question: Take absolutely any triangle, split each of its three angles into three equal parts, and the points where neighbouring trisectors cross will always form a perfect equilateral triangle.

question: A patient with Capgras delusion is gripped by which specific belief?
choices: That they themselves have died and no longer exist
That a total stranger is a loved one wearing a disguise
That they are slowly turning into an animal
That their close family have been secretly swapped for identical impostors
anchorText: has been replaced by an identical impostor

question: There is a rare condition, caused by damage to the brain's visual cortex, in which people are completely blind yet sincerely insist they can still see, even inventing descriptions of things that are not in front of them.
anchorText: that they are capable of seeing

question: Brain damage can leave a person unable to perceive motion at all - a poured cup of tea looks frozen in mid-air - even though they still see stationary objects perfectly clearly.
anchorText: cannot perceive motion in their visual field, despite being able to see stationary objects without issue

question: There is a recognised psychiatric condition, documented even in mass-panic outbreaks, in which people become overwhelmingly convinced that their genitals are retracting into the body and about to disappear.
anchorText: an overpowering belief that their sex organs are retracting and will disappear

question: In a 'false pregnancy' (pseudocyesis) the woman only imagines she is pregnant; her body produces no real physical signs of pregnancy at all.
anchorText: tender breasts with secretions, abdominal growth, delayed menstrual periods, and subjective feelings of a moving fetus
